On-Chain Operator. Lesson 13.5, Scaling, compounding and the annual review. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You already have a balance sheet. Income is only the part of it you can explain after losses.
Compounding: reinvesting the retained share grows principal, and income with it.
At a 4.66% risk-adjusted yield with 30% retained, principal grows ~1.4%/yr from retention alone.
The payout grows at about the same rate: $16,310 → ~$17,480 after five years (before any new capital).
Scaling rules as the book grows: Caps are percentages, so position sizes rise, and so does market impact.
Check pool depth and exit liquidity at the new size.
Add independent protocols and issuers before adding size to existing ones.
More size means more value at stake in custody: revisit Module 12.2.
Balance sheet: start vs end equity, LTV, runway 2.
Losses and near-misses: what happened, what changed 4.
Risk assumptions: update loss probabilities from the year's incidents 6.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Retained income reinvested per policy. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Exit liquidity checked at current size. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Annual review completed and filed with the books. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
Check yourself. 1. Yield 5%, 40% retained. Growth from retention alone? The answer: ~2% a year.
Check yourself. 2. Why check exit liquidity as the book grows? The answer: A position that was easy to exit at $50k may move the market at $500k.
Check yourself. 3. What should the annual review update? The answer: Loss-probability assumptions, from the year's incidents and near-misses.
